Based on the chest X-ray showing a ground-glass appearance and air bronchograms in a 32-week preterm infant, the clinical picture strongly supports a diagnosis of Respiratory Distress Syndrome. The normal complete blood count and lack of fever or purulent sputum make a bacterial pneumonia less likely.
